notes: v534 — 🚀 Breakout and 🥇 Vol record now mean a FIXED thing. Both used to be measured against “the highest since the stored history begins” — so their meaning quietly changed every time the pantry got deeper. When the server went from one year of history to three, a breakout silently became a THREE-year high, and Vol record had nearly stopped firing at all because it needed a three-year volume record. From now on: Breakout = a ONE-YEAR price high; Vol record = a THREE-MONTH volume record. Stable definitions that mean the same thing next year as today — and they match the wording the lessons always used. This also makes the three-year durability study a fair comparison, since every era is now measured with the same yardstick. Needs the matching server update, and the era study should be re-run afterwards. Hard-refresh (Ctrl+F5).
